headline: CASCADIA CARMACKS: BEST HOLE EVER — 75.55m @ 2.18% CuEq STEPS OUT 100m INTO UNTESTED YUKON COPPER-GOLD ZONE
snippet: Cascadia Minerals Ltd. announced October 1 that drill hole CD-26-058 at the Zone 2000S of the road-accessible Carmacks copper-gold project in central Yukon returned 75.55 metres averaging 1.19% copper, 0.97 g/t gold, 10.4 g/t silver and 335 ppm molybdenum (2.18% CuEq) — one of the highest-grade intersections in the project's history. The hole sits 100 metres northeast of the previous best result and confirms significant step-out potential; a sub-interval of 48.66 metres graded 3.03% CuEq including 1.61% Cu and 1.39 g/t Au. Six additional holes await assay, with drilling continuing until mid-October. For copper-focused junior investors, a property-record intersection in a zone that remains open to expansion — at a Tier 1 Yukon address with road access and proximity to grid power — is the definition of a re-rating catalyst in the current copper supply squeeze.

headline: CHILE COPPER FALLS TO 15-YEAR LOW: AUGUST OUTPUT 369,500T, DOWN 12.8% — WORSE THAN THE 2017 ESCONDIDA STRIKE
snippet: Chile's August 2026 copper output fell to 369,500 tonnes — 12.8% below August 2025 and the country's lowest monthly production since February 2011, according to Chile's National Statistics Institute (INE). That reading is worse than any month during the 2017 Escondida strike, which markets had previously used as the benchmark for Chilean supply stress. State miner Cochilco has cut its 2026 full-year forecast to 5.27 million tonnes, down roughly 7% from 2025, citing severe winter weather, declining ore grades, port disruptions, and operational mishaps at multiple major sites. Chile supplies approximately a quarter of global copper mine output. For junior copper investors, the August data arrives alongside active labour disputes at Escondida and Centinela and the Cobre Panama recommended closure — building the most complete simultaneous supply-constraint case for copper since the energy-transition surge of 2022.

headline: NEXMETALS SELEBI MAIN +72%: 32.47 MT @ 1.53% Cu, 0.98% Ni — 1.77 BILLION LB CuEq IN BOTSWANA, COBALT NOW REPORTED
snippet: NexMetals Mining Corp. (TSX-V: NEXM) announced October 1 that its updated Selebi Main Mineral Resource Estimate has grown 72% to 32.47 million tonnes in the Inferred category, grading 1.53% copper, 0.98% nickel and 0.05% cobalt — containing 495,400 tonnes of copper and 316,800 tonnes of nickel for a combined 1.77 billion pounds copper equivalent. 91% of the tonnage increase is attributable to new drilling in the Flexure Zone, which extended the known mineralized envelope. The adjacent Selebi North estimate is pending, and the 2026 Selebi Main MRE will be supported by a NI 43-101 Technical Report filed within 45 days. The past-producing Selebi mine in Botswana benefits from established infrastructure. For base metal investors, a 72% resource expansion at a past-producing southern African copper-nickel mine — with cobalt now added as a third payable metal — is a substantial pre-PEA re-rating event at current metal prices.

headline: AMAROQ NANOQ: 33 HOLES COMPLETE, 88% VISIBLE GOLD, 97–99% MET RECOVERY — GREENLAND RESOURCE DRILL WRAPS UP
snippet: Amaroq Minerals Ltd. (LSE/TSX: AMRQ) announced October 1 the completion of its 2026 resource drilling programme at the Nanoq Gold Project in South Greenland — 4,728.9 metres across 33 holes focused on infill drilling of the Central Zone alongside step-out holes to the south and West 1 target. Approximately 88% of holes intersected visible gold and copper sulphides consistent with 2024–2025 observations. Initial metallurgical test work by SGS Lakefield returned total gold recoveries of 97–99% using the existing Nalunaq processing flowsheet, confirming that Nanoq ore is amenable for treatment at the company's operating Nalunaq mill without modification. Construction of a beach landing facility and starter access track is underway. Assay results are pending. For Greenland gold investors, a near-perfect drill success rate combined with confirmed mill compatibility and infrastructure development underway sets up a maiden Mineral Resource Estimate as the next catalyst.

headline: GOLDEN CARIBOO FIRST RESOURCE: 995K OZ GOLD INFERRED + 175K INDICATED AT BC'S QUESNELLE — OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS
snippet: Golden Cariboo Resources (CSE: GCC) announced September 30 its inaugural NI 43-101 resource at the past-producing Quesnelle Gold Quartz Mine in central British Columbia: 10 million tonnes at 0.55 g/t Au for 175,000 oz gold Indicated, and 70.9 million tonnes at 0.44 g/t Au for 995,000 oz gold Inferred — a combined 1.19 million gold equivalent ounces. The estimate covers the Halo and North Hixon zones across 1,150 metres of strike and 420 metres width, based on just 24 diamond drill holes totalling 8,466 metres; the deposit remains open in all directions. Average silver grades of 1.2–1.5 g/t add byproduct value. CEO Frank Callaghan described the deposit as 'a sleeping giant we've only begun to wake up.' For Canadian junior gold investors, a near-million-ounce inferred at a historically producing BC property with expansion potential in all directions — derived from only 24 holes — is exactly the pre-financing setup that attracts institutional capital at current gold prices.

headline: USA RARE EARTH CEO SWAP: THRAS MORAITIS (EX-SERRA VERDE) TAKES COMMAND OCT. 1 — INTEGRATION BEGINS AT LARGEST U.S. REE PLATFORM
snippet: USA Rare Earth Inc. (Nasdaq: USAR) completed its CEO succession on October 1, with Thras Moraitis — architect of the company's recent combination with Serra Verde Group and former Serra Verde CEO since January 2023 — formally assuming the top role from outgoing CEO Barbara Humpton. The combined entity holds the Round Top hard rock rare earth deposit in Texas alongside Serra Verde's ionic clay assets in Brazil, giving USAR one of the broadest rare earth development platforms outside China in the Western world. Moraitis' stated near-term focus: operational integration, reliable supply to U.S. and allied defense customers, and improving execution. For Western rare earth investors, a proven ionic clay operator taking direct control of a combined U.S.-Brazil REE platform — on the same day Lynas acquired Meteoric Resources for A$968M — underlines the consolidation wave now reshaping non-Chinese rare earth supply chains.

headline: GOLDSEEK SWOT: RAMELIUS RAISES FY30 TARGET 5%, SHANDONG CUTS CHINA OUTPUT 26% — PRODUCER DIVERGENCE WIDENS
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis highlights a diverging producer landscape: on the bullish side, Ramelius Resources (ASX: RMS) raised its FY30 production target to 560,000–610,000 oz (up 5% on higher Mt Magnet grades), projecting A$1.5–1.8B in free cash flow through FY30; on the bearish side, Shandong Gold Mining (SHA: 600547) cut its 2026 production target to 36–38 tonnes from at least 49 tonnes previously — a 22–26% reduction — citing tighter Chinese government safety requirements at domestic mines, while Kinross Gold (TSX: K) trimmed 2026–2027 guidance 8% to 1.84–1.86 Moz on La Coipa weather disruption and Round Mountain grade misses, offsetting the cut with a raised capital return target of 50% of free cash flow. For investors assessing where mining equity leverage is most compelling, the ASX mid-tier producers raising long-dated guidance contrast sharply with major Chinese and North American seniors constrained by operational headwinds.

headline: LITHIUM SLIDES BEFORE GOLDEN WEEK: SQM -1.8%, CHINA FUTURES DOWN THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION TO $17,660/T
snippet: Chile's SQM (NYSE: SQM) fell 1.83% to US$64.87 on October 1 as China's lithium-carbonate futures contract slid 0.94% to 118,420 yuan (approximately US$17,660/tonne) — its third consecutive daily decline after drops of 5.69% Monday and 1.69% Tuesday. Chinese lithium and battery markets will not trade again until October 8 after China's Golden Week national holiday, removing the main price-discovery mechanism for a week. Traders read the move as supply catching up with battery demand ahead of the holiday, with no fresh restocking signal expected before mid-October. Albemarle (NYSE: ALB) also traded lower. For lithium mining investors, the pre-holiday positioning adds to an already-challenged narrative: while Morgan Stanley forecasts an 80,000-tonne LCE deficit in 2026, current futures prices suggest the market is not pricing that deficit in yet — creating a contested entry point heading into Q4 demand data.

headline: KUYA SILVER MINING FORUM: $30M CASH, ZERO DEBT, 20,000m DRILL PLAN — BETHANIA TARGETS 1 MOZ SILVER/YEAR
snippet: Kuya Silver Corp. (TSX-V: KUYA) used its Mining Forum Americas 2026 appearance on September 30 to outline a growth plan built around the producing Bethania silver mine in Peru: the Camila mill is being expanded from 150 to 250 tonnes per day, a 20,000-metre drilling program — the first major campaign at Bethania in five years — has commenced, and management holds more than CAD $30 million in cash with zero debt and no near-term financing requirement. At a silver price assumption of CAD $60/oz (silver spot is roughly CAD $84 at current rates), management says margins at 1 million oz/year production would be 'very, very expansive.' The Bethania mine is fully permitted up to 350 t/d. For retail silver investors looking for a de-risked, producing Peru silver asset with balance sheet strength at a time when silver has pulled back 50% from its January 2026 record high, Kuya offers an unusual combination of production plus exploration upside plus zero leverage.
